text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar said the government will try to achieve an annual growth of 30 percent in exports.
- An unrealistic revenue target of 341 billion rupees for 1996/97 (July-June) against the 264 billion 1995/96 target is expected to be revised after restructuring of import tariffs.

- At least 129 people, including 50 women and children, were killed and more than 105 were injured in a passenger train accident near Khanewal in central Pakistan. Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has ordered a judicial enquiry.
- A bomb partly damaged the office of evening newspaper Qaumi Akhbar in Karachi.
- Moderate earthquakes jolted Peshawar, Harnai and Sibi and other parts of Balochistan.
- Bangladesh foreign minister Abdus Samad Azad arrived in Islamabad for talks with his counterpart Gohar Ayub.
- Pakistan expects a lenient approach regarding realisation of macro-economic targets from the International Monetary Fund review mission reaching Islamabad on Thursday.
- Some 92 percent of Pakistan's sea freight bill, estimated at $1.5 billion, goes to foreign ships as the Pakistani-flagged merchant fleet has shrunk to 24 ships from 74 in 1992.
- Pakistan will close down five missions abroad due to financial constraints.
